Baram v0.7.6 lets you save the look you have set up — colours, appearance settings and
hidden bars — as a theme package you can give to someone else, and install such a package
from a file. The editor's fonts, font size and line height join the appearance dials, so a
theme can suggest them too, and line width can now be set in characters. Plugin authors get a
developer mode for loading a plugin from a folder in the released app, and the marketplace
now says who distributes each plugin.

If you are updating from v0.7.5, these are the changes most likely to catch you out:
**Font Family, Code Font, Font Size and Line Height now work like the other dials**, so one
you had changed shows **Custom** and a revert button, and font size and line height values
appear at the right of their rows instead of in the description; **Line width is shown in
characters** rather than pixels, and in the settings search results it is an **Open...**
button instead of a pixel slider; **the settings window is wider**; the formatting toolbar
**shows icons instead of letters**, and the fold arrows beside headings, lists and toggles
are chevrons; on the Installed tab of Settings › Plugins, the **Community** section is now
called **From the registry**; and in the Korean interface the Zettel settings tab is now
**제텔**. If you go back to v0.7.5 after updating, it shows Baram's defaults for the four font
settings, because this version moves them to where v0.7.5 does not look.

---

# New and improved

## Share your look as a theme

**Export Look as Theme...**, next to **Import Theme...** in Settings › Appearance, saves what
you see now as a theme package (`.zip`):

- the colours of the theme you are using, or Baram's default light and dark palettes if you
  use **System (Auto)**;
- every appearance dial whose current value differs from Baram's default, including Font
  Family, Code Font, Font Size and Line Height (Code Font Size and Code Line Height are not
  dials and are not included);
- and, if you tick **Also suggest hiding the bars I hid**, the bars you have hidden.

The screen lists all of this before you save, under the names the settings rows use; Line
width is shown there in pixels rather than characters. A theme's own CSS, and any font files
it ships, are not included. A package that carries settings or hidden bars can be installed
only by the version of Baram that exported it, or a newer one. Installing a package from a
file is new in this version, so whoever you give one to needs v0.7.6 or later.

## Install a theme from a file

**Import Theme...** used to read only a colour settings file (`.json`), and the only way to
install a theme package was the theme registry. It now takes a theme package too, and tells
the two apart by their content rather than the file extension. A package gets the same
checks on its contents and the same consent dialog as a theme from the registry, and then
appears in the gallery. If a theme with the same id is already installed, Baram asks before
replacing it, and says so when the replacement means that theme will stop receiving updates
from the theme registry. A theme installed from a file does not receive registry updates. A
package over 32 MB is refused.

**Import Theme...** now reads the file you pick wherever it is. In v0.7.5 a colour settings file
outside the folders and files you had open in Baram failed with “Could not read or parse the
file”.

## Fonts join the appearance dials

**Font Family**, **Code Font**, **Font Size** and **Line Height** (Settings › Editor, under
Font) now work like the dials under Display. A theme can suggest a value for each, and the
row then shows **Theme**; a value you set shows **Custom** with its own revert. If you had
changed any of the four, the update keeps your value and marks it Custom; one you never
changed stays on Baram's default. Font Size, Line Height, Code Font Size and Code Line Height
now show their value at the right of the row.

A font name you type is now accepted only up to 128 characters and without control
characters. A name that breaks either rule is not saved, and the update drops one that was
saved before.

When the theme you are using ships a font of its own, the font rows now label that font
**From theme**, where they used to say **Not on this machine** unless the font was also
installed on your computer.

## Line width in characters

**Line width** (Settings › Editor, under Display) now says how many characters fit on a line.
It measures your body font at its size, with your letter spacing and editor padding, using
the width of 가 when the interface is in Korean and the average of a–z when it is in English.
Its slider runs from 20 to 120 characters, and its far left is **No limit**. The width itself
is still saved in pixels, so changing the font changes the count, not the width. The menu
beside the slider switches the row to **Pixels**, and the row shows pixels whenever the
character width cannot be measured.

## A clearer theme gallery

The theme cards in Settings › Appearance draw a larger preview, which now also shows the
selection, the cursor and the theme's warning, success and danger colours. A theme with both
a light and a dark palette shows the two side by side, where the card used to show only the
light one, and the **System (Auto)** card is drawn from Baram's actual default palettes
instead of hand-picked colours. Each card names its modes — **Light**, **Dark** or **Light · Dark** — and a theme
you installed also shows its author, version and description.

The settings window is wider to make room: 880 pixels instead of 720. It also shrinks to fit a
narrow app window, which the old fixed width did not.

## Where each plugin comes from

The marketplace now says who distributes each plugin. A plugin Baram publishes there carries
a **Baram** badge on its card, on its detail page and on the Installed tab, and its install
dialog says **Distributed by Baram**. A plugin you installed before this version shows no
badge on the Installed tab or on its detail page until its next update. Built-in plugins,
which ship inside the app, have no badge.

Baram now also reads a separate community list. When this version was released, that list
had no plugins yet. Once it has some, a plugin from it is marked **Community** with its
publisher's GitHub account, its install dialog says that Baram does not review its code, and
this version installs it only if it runs sandboxed. Baram remembers which account published
a community plugin you installed: if an update comes from a different GitHub account, Baram
asks you again before installing it, even when it asks for no new permissions, and says what
changed. If Baram cannot load the community list and has not loaded it since it started (a
missing list counts as empty), Browse still lists Baram's own plugins and says “Community
plugins could not be loaded — only Baram's own plugins are listed. ↻ Refresh tries again.”
If it has loaded the list before, it keeps showing that list instead.

The **Community** section of the Installed tab is now **From the registry**. It holds every
plugin you installed from the marketplace, Baram's own included, as it always did.

## Developer mode for plugin authors

Loading a plugin straight from a folder used to need a development build of Baram. The
**Developer** section at the bottom of Settings › Plugins now has a **Developer mode**
switch, and turning it on asks you to confirm first. With it on, the folder button beside
**Load dev plugin folder** opens a folder picker, and the plugin asks for its permissions, in
the same kind of dialog an install shows, before any of its code runs.

- Only sandboxed plugins load this way. A folder is also refused if its plugin id starts
  with `baram-`, belongs to a plugin you have installed, or already has data stored under it
  by another plugin — for example, one you uninstalled.
- A folder you loaded loads again at the next start without asking, as long as it asks for
  nothing beyond what you approved. If it now asks for more, it waits until you press
  **Reload** and approve.
- While developer mode is on, the marketplace will not install a plugin whose id one of your
  folders has taken.
- Turning developer mode off unloads the folders' plugins at once.

## Settings search finds rows it used to miss

Search in the settings window did not know about twenty-six rows that were already in the
settings tabs, so they could be reached only by opening their tab — among them **Vim
Keybindings**, most of the Journal, Zettel and AI settings, **Code Font Size**, **Code Line
Height** and the update settings. It finds them now. Most switches, choices and sliders can
be changed right in the results; the others have an **Open...** button that takes you to
them.

## One set of icons

Across the sidebars, panels, dialogs, tab bar, menus and the editor margin, icons that were
drawn with text characters and emoji — `×`, `▸`, `⚠`, `●`, `★` and the like — are now drawn
from the icon set most of the app already used, so they share a size and line weight and
take the theme's colours. The formatting toolbar that appears over a selection shows icons
instead of the letters B, I, S, H1, UL and the rest, with the same tooltips, and the fold
arrows beside headings, lists and toggles are chevrons.

Buttons that were drawn as a symbol, such as Pull and Push in the Source Control panel, now
have a translated name that screen readers can read. The dot on a tab with unsaved changes is
labelled “Unsaved changes”, and the tick beside the current choice in the table and formula
right-click menus and in the block menu's **Turn into** list is labelled “Selected”. In HTML
and PDF exports, toggle arrows are chevrons too.

# Fixed

## Settings

- **Settings search described the Archive after setting as picking up tasks finished “more
  than null days ago”.** It now shows the number you set.
- **The row you drag while reordering the activity bar in Settings › Layout** is now dimmed
  while you drag it. Before, it looked like the other rows.

## Skills

- **In a skill's Dependencies section, a required skill that cannot be found** is shown in
  red and laid out like the rest of the list. It used to lose both.

## Korean interface

- **The Korean interface now calls the Zettel space 제텔** where it said Zettel: the settings
  tab, its section heading and its rows' labels and descriptions, the description of the
  Tasks home setting, the activity bar, the shortcut category, the hub's new-note button and
  setup message, Quick Capture's error messages, and the notices about the space and its
  folder. The folder picker's title, which said Zettelkasten, now says 제텔 too. The menu and
  two shortcut names already said 제텔. Command palette entries such as “Zettel
  Perspective”, and the New Zettel dialog, are still in English.

---

**Updating.** Press **Install & Restart** in the update dialog and Baram installs in place
and restarts. Linux `.deb` and `.rpm` cannot be updated in place by the updater; those, and
any install that fails, open the releases page instead.
